learn.title: Moving on the number line
learn.body: Adding a positive number moves you right. Adding a negative number moves you left. Start at 2 and add $-5$: you move 5 steps left and land on $-3$. So $2+(-5)=-3$.

learn.title: Same signs, different signs
learn.body: Same signs: add the sizes and keep the sign, so $-3+(-5)=-8$. Different signs: subtract the smaller size from the larger and keep the sign of the larger one, so $7+(-10)=-3$ (10 is bigger, and it is negative).

learn.title: Subtracting is adding the opposite
learn.body: To subtract a number, add its opposite instead. $4-(-6)$ becomes $4+6=10$. And $-2-5$ becomes $-2+(-5)=-7$. This one trick turns every subtraction into an addition.

learn.title: Work out $-4-(-7)$
learn.body: Turn the subtraction into an addition, then use the sign rules.
steps: Different signs, so subtract the sizes: $7-4=3$.
The larger size (7) is positive, so the answer is $3$.

learn.body: Two minus signs in a row make a plus. $5-(-2)$ is the same as $5+2$.

questions.explanation: Same signs: add the sizes, 3 and 5 make 8, and keep the minus sign.
$5-8=5+(-8)$. Different signs, so $8-5=3$, and the larger size is negative: $-3$.
Subtracting $-6$ is the same as adding its opposite, $6$. So $4+6=10$.
Same signs: $12+8=20$, and both are negative, so $-20$.

questions.prompt: Match each sum with its value.
questions.explanation: Check the signs first. Same signs add the sizes; different signs subtract them.

questions.prompt: Work out $8-(-3)$. Put the steps in order.
steps: Rewrite subtraction as adding the opposite
questions.explanation: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding a positive.
